tasks.title: Determinant of a 3×3 matrix
tasks.why: On every paper and pure routine, so it's cheap points.
recipe: Pick the row or column with the most zeros.
Expand: \(\det A=\sum_j (-1)^{i+j}a_{ij}M_{ij}\), where \(M_{ij}\) deletes row \(i\) and column \(j\).
Check the sign pattern \(+,-,+\) before adding.

tasks.title: Inverse of a 2×2 matrix
tasks.why: One formula. The only trap is forgetting to check that \(\det\ne0\).
recipe: Compute \(\det=ad-bc\). If it is 0, there is no inverse.

tasks.title: Eigenvalues and definiteness of a symmetric 2×2 matrix
tasks.why: Worth more than the first two, but needs the characteristic polynomial done carefully.
recipe: All \(\lambda>0\): positive definite. Any \(\lambda<0\) together with one \(>0\): indefinite.

T1.question: Compute \(\det\begin{pmatrix}1&2&0\\0&1&3\\2&0&1\end{pmatrix}\).
T1.solution:
1. Expand along row 1 (it has a zero): \(1\cdot\det\begin{pmatrix}1&3\\0&1\end{pmatrix}-2\cdot\det\begin{pmatrix}0&3\\2&1\end{pmatrix}+0\).
  2. \(=1\cdot1-2\cdot(0-6)=1+12=\mathbf{13}\).

Rubric (4, inferred): 2 for the expansion with signs, 2 for the value.

T3.question: Let \(A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}\). Find the eigenvalues and decide whether \(A\) is positive definite.
T3.solution:
1. \(\operatorname{tr}A=4\), \(\det A=3\), so \(\lambda^2-4\lambda+3=0\).
  2. \(\lambda=1\) or \(\lambda=3\).
  3. Both are \(>0\), and none is \(<0\), so \(A\) is positive definite.

Rubric (6, inferred): 2 polynomial, 2 eigenvalues, 2 conclusion with reason.
